clearedSpotChecks.check: Arc: USDC is the native asset with 18 decimals and also answers at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 with 6 decimals. The face rounds down, so a settle bracket on the face can credit one face unit for less than 10^12 base units. How much can an ordinary account take that way.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I repeated the chain reads and derived the bound by hand. At Arc block 32,608,962 eth_getBalance of the PoolManager returned 2,431,185,769,228,410,246,667,475 and balanceOf(PoolManager) on 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 returned 2,431,185,769,228, which is the floor of the first figure divided by 10^12. With a state override of the PoolManager balance, balanceOf returned 0 for 999,999,999,999 base units and 1 for 10^12, so the face rounds down as the item says. An eth_call of transfer(0xdEaD, 1) on the face with the PoolManager as sender returned true, so the face can pay out, and a plain 1 unit value call to the PoolManager reverted. Code: the credit is the checked rise of balanceOf since sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 358-364) and settle rejects msg.value while an ERC-20 is synced (356). Bound: with S = 10^12, native balance N at sync, inflows I and native takes T inside one bracket, the credit C is floor((N + I - T) / S) - floor(N / S), so C * S - I is below S. Face transfers move multiples of S and give C * S = I exactly, so a gain needs a native inflow that is not a multiple of S while the face is synced. settle and settleFor are the only payable functions in src/ outside src/test and there is no receive or fallback function, so that inflow has to be a SELFDESTRUCT. https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences says SELFDESTRUCT is allowed and moves the balance to the beneficiary, which settles the part the item left untested. https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/gas-and-fees says the 20 gwei minimum base fee is a floor enforced by the protocol, and eth_feeHistory returned 20 gwei for the last six blocks. Any single warm CALL costs at least 100 gas, which is 2 * 10^12 base units at the floor and already exceeds the largest gain of one bracket, and a full round with sync, a value call, SELFDESTRUCT, settle and take costs several hundred times that. An ordinary account therefore loses money on every round. The same docs page says the base fee is paid to the block beneficiary, so a block proposer gets its own base fee back. That residual needs the operator role and is capped at 0.000001 USDC per round, about 0.001 USDC per 30,000,000 gas block at roughly 30,000 gas per round. I did not measure the gas of a full round.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Tempo: from hardfork T5 three precompiles on the Implicit Approval List (FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP20ChannelReserve) may move TIP-20 tokens out of any account without an allowance through system_transfer_from. Can an ordinary account make one of them pull tokens out of the PoolManager, which would lower a balance without a take.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the six files at commit 697ea97 from raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo and read every call of system_transfer_from. The function is a plain Rust method that the ABI dispatch does not expose, and from T5 it returns Unauthorized unless the caller is on IMPLICIT_APPROVAL_LIST, which holds the fee manager, the stablecoin DEX and the channel reserve (tip20/mod.rs:939-980, address_registry/mod.rs:27-46). There are five production call sites: stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:301 inside transfer_from, tip_fee_manager/amm.rs:239 and 360, and tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs:215 and 380. The DEX reaches transfer_from only through decrement_balance_or_transfer_from at lines 428, 494, 710 and 913, and the dispatcher passes msg_sender as the sender for place, placeFlip and both swaps (stablecoin_dex/dispatch.rs:26-66). The follow-up order of a filled flip order uses the internal DEX balance only (stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:1093-1112 and the internal_balance_only branch at 897-912), so a fill by a third party does not pull from a wallet. The AMM and the channel reserve pass msg_sender at all four sites. The dispatch tables of the fee manager and the channel reserve have no entry for transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address), unlockCallback or an IHooks selector, and the DEX balanceOf takes two arguments, so the PoolManager cannot be the direct caller of a pulling function with the call shapes it issues (src/types/Currency.sol:60-73, 94; src/PoolManager.sol:110; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-137). Fee collection before a transaction takes a fee_payer argument (tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:158-177) and I did not read the handler that supplies it, so that one link rests on the item's statement. The source comment at tip20/mod.rs:948-949 confirms that pulling only from msg.sender is enforced per call site, so the item's caveat about later additions to the list stands.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Exhaustive search for a sequence of unlock, sync, settle, settleFor, take, clear, mint, burn, ERC-6909 transfer and direct payment by one account that leaves the account richer or the PoolManager short, in seven currency settings.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read settle_model.py against the source and reran it. The model's account_delta matches _accountDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:368-378), its settle branch matches lines 349-364 including the NonzeroNativeValue revert and the checked subtraction, sync has no lock check (279-288), and take debits before paying (291-297). Runs of settings 0 to 4 with one account, claim cap 2 and delta cap 4 gave 35,859, 31,628, 9,709, 208,972 and 48,488 states. Only setting 3, the scaled face with forced native sends, showed a gain (13 of 13 base units in the toy). The research text lists 48,488 for the scaled face without forced sends and gives no state count for setting 3, which is a small omission. I also checked the two facts the one to one settings rest on. Celo block 83,472,704: eth_getBalance of the PoolManager and balanceOf on 0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438 both returned 0x14e4fa625268c856de6, transfer(0xdEaD, 1) on the token with the PoolManager as sender returned true, and the token source reads balanceOf as the account balance and moves value through the transfer precompile without calling the recipient (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-monorepo/master/packages/protocol/contracts/common/GoldToken.sol, _transfer and balanceOf; I did not confirm that master equals the deployed implementation). Polygon, latest block on 2026-11-22: eth_getBalance and balanceOf on 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 both returned 0x292aafe302508c4d5d195, and transfer(0xdEaD, 1) with the PoolManager as sender returned 32 bytes of zero, which Currency.transfer treats as failure (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74), while amount 0 returned true. So the CELO token is a one to one face that can pay out and 0x1010 is one that cannot, as modelled. My own reading of the double credit path agrees with the search: a native credit needs the currency slot to be zero (353-354), an ERC-20 credit needs the slot to hold the token with reserves taken at that sync (358-360), sync writes both slots together and sync(address(0)) clears only the currency (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32), so one inflow cannot be booked under both ids. The model caps amounts at 2 and deltas at 4, so it is evidence for the logic and says nothing about widths, which item 9 covers by reading.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Arc: the CallFrom precompile at 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000003 starts a call on behalf of Memo and Multicall3From. Does that inner call run with transient storage of its own, which would separate PoolManager deltas from payouts inside one unlock, and can a contract in the middle of a transaction use it to act as another account at the PoolManager.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read init_subcall in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs (lines 884-960 of the file as fetched). It rejects any scheme other than CALL, rejects a static context, rejects value, and rejects a child caller that differs from both the calling contract and the transaction sender with the message 'sender spoofing requires tx.origin as sender'. The registry allows only Memo and Multicall3From to call the precompile (evm.rs:1666-1676). The item left Multicall3From unread. I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/contracts/src/batch/Multicall3From.sol: every entry point passes msg.sender to _callFrom (lines 43, 58, 81, 161), and Memo.sol line 43 does the same. A contract that gains control inside someone else's transaction and calls either helper is therefore presented as itself, fails the check, and cannot act as the signer or as the PoolManager at src/ERC6909.sol:25-64 or src/PoolManager.sol:300-336. https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/batched-transactions states the same rule. The child frame is built on the same journal after a checkpoint (evm.rs:1031-1040), which fits the item's statement on transient storage. Like the item, I read the main branch and did not confirm which release mainnet runs, and I did not read where revm keeps transient storage.

clearedSpotChecks.check: A stale sync: sync needs no lock, and its two slots are the only settlement state that can outlive an unlock. What can a party gain from a sync left behind inside one transaction, and what would follow if a network failed to wipe transient storage between transactions.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The code reading holds. unlock leaves the flag false and the counter at zero or reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:105-113), so the synced currency and reserves are the only settlement state that can outlive a call (279-288). A stale ERC-20 sync makes a later settle with msg.value revert (356) and lets the next settle without a fresh sync book the rise since the stale sync (358-364). One sentence needs a qualifier: the item says that inside one transaction the rise can only be the caller's own payment or an inflow it triggered. A transaction can carry operations of several users, for example an ERC-4337 bundle. The conclusion survives that case, because a later user that pays an ERC-20 through sync, transfer and settle overwrites the stale slots at its own sync (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32) and a later user that pays native value without sync(address(0)) reverts at line 356 and loses only gas. The comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 names this denial of service. I add a low priority lead for it. I found no path by which the stale slot gives one user another user's payment.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Which invariants of flash accounting and custody does the code enforce, and where. This is the list that the other items of this unit try to break.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read every line the item cites without reference to any other copy of the code. Lock: set at src/PoolManager.sol:107, cleared at 113, checked by onlyWhenUnlocked at 96-99 on modifyLiquidity, swap, donate, take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint and burn. sync, initialize, updateDynamicLPFee, the ERC-6909 functions and the protocol fee functions carry no lock check and write no delta. Counter: _accountDelta at 368-378 returns on zero, decrements when the slot reaches zero and increments when it leaves zero, and CurrencyDelta.applyDelta uses a checked int256 addition on one slot per (account, currency) for both read and write (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41). Credits and debits are as listed: settle (349-364), burn against a checked claim decrease (332-336, src/ERC6909.sol:85-89, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22), take and mint debits before the external effect (294-295, 326-327), clear only for an exact positive match (310-319). Hook deltas are subtracted from the caller in the same step, so caller plus hook equals what Pool returned (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:230, 242, 306-313). The only outgoing value paths are Currency.transfer at src/PoolManager.sol:295 and src/ProtocolFees.sol:56. A grep of src/ outside src/test finds payable only on settle and settleFor and no receive or fallback function. The unchecked blocks at 292, 316 and 323 contain no arithmetic that can wrap, since toInt128 reverts at 2^127 (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59) and the called functions keep their own checked arithmetic. I also ran the unit's keccak.py: none of the 13 selectors the PoolManager sends equals one of its 33 external selectors, which supports the self call item. The item treats the amounts Pool computes as given. That part belongs to the swap, liquidity and bit level units and I did not check it here.

leads.question: On each network, do the deployed routers and position managers call sync(address(0)) before a native settle, and can operations of different users run inside one transaction there (ERC-4337 EntryPoint bundles, sponsored or batched transaction types)?
leads.why: sync needs no lock and its two transient slots survive until the transaction ends (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). An ERC-20 sync left by an earlier operation in the same transaction makes a later settle with msg.value revert with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), and the comment at line 348 says integrators should sync first. The settlement unit cleared the stale sync for a transaction of one party. With several users in one transaction the effect on the later user is a reverted operation and lost gas, with no transfer of funds, so this is a griefing path against native payers whose router skips the sync.
